brief_rationale: The trajectory meets all responsibility chain requirements with no serious or minor chain errors. All safety-critical items including medication reconciliation, cardiovascular risk recognition, red flag screening, and concrete follow-up planning were addressed. Two high-order points (HO1 and HO2) were completed with meaningful impact: communication was adapted to the caregiver's anxiety and conflict, and the plan was navigated through real-world constraints (family disagreement, work schedule). However, only two high-order points were completed (not three), so the trajectory does not reach Perfect.

closure_assessment.explanation: The episode reached safe closure with an executable plan: medications reconciled with specific timing (aspirin morning, atorvastatin bedtime, continuing nifedipine and mecobalamin), cardiology follow-up completed with new prescriptions, ophthalmology follow-up scheduled, home BP monitoring initiated, and clear emergency thresholds. Family confirmed understanding and demonstrated ability to execute.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO3 is complete: doctor queried workspace records, correctly distinguished sinus rhythm with ECG abnormalities from confirmed atrial fibrillation (no AF confirmed), and integrated findings into the follow-up plan specifying what to ask the cardiologist.

HO4 was not triggered: no new neurologic symptoms, other-eye symptoms, chest pain, or execution failures emerged during the trajectory. The patient remained stable throughout, so no reprioritization was required.
